# #4540: Patch: the fuzz monitor fails a game in which a target drawn at random is one its card could not have chosen by hand
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some cards make their choices at random. A spell cast at random picks its own targets, and while a certain Unit is on the field every target is drawn at random. The rules say a random draw may land only on a card a player could have picked by hand, so a spell must never land on a Unit that spells can't target. A bug of exactly this kind was fixed two days ago: random casts were stealing or hitting such Units, or wasting a pick on one and doing nothing. The fuzz plays thousands of random games every day and never saw it, because a wasted pick leaves no trace in the game's record. Once this is built, the fuzz checks every random target pick against the targeting rules. The next bug of this kind, in any card, is then caught by the daily run instead of by a player.

## Why
- R452 (`spec/rulings/R0452.md`, its last sentence) says a random cast's `target` prompt draws only from the options the targeting point leaves. So it never picks an Evasive card in play (R4353002), a Unit Immune to Spells or a Dormant card (R1839000). R4353002 and R1200 say the same of a Mayor's random declared targets.
- #4500 (`f5a5cc1ffa`, 2026-11-22) fixed `cast_prompt_shape` (`crates/engine/src/prompts.rs:1292`), which answered a random cast's prompts from options nobody had filtered. Hand-built tests found the bug: `r4353002_random_cast_never_picks_evasive_enemy_unit` and `r452_random_cast_never_picks_immune_to_spells_unit_or_dormant_unit`, at `crates/engine/tests/rules/effects_cast.rs:1010` and `:1060`. The fuzz did not.
- No invariant can see such a pick today:
  - `answer_at_random` (`prompts.rs:1364`) emits nothing; its comment says 'Nothing is emitted, since no prompt was open'.
  - A declared target drawn at random goes straight into the run's targets: `random_targets::draw_picks` at `play_steps.rs:2511`, `cry_trigger.rs:339` and `play_choices.rs:2404`, and `random_picks` at `play_steps.rs:2527` and `cry_trigger.rs:367`.
  - The twenty checks in `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` never read Evasive or Immune to Spells as targeting. A grep for `evasive_bars` or `immune_to_spells` there finds nothing; Evasive appears only in I17's Defense half.
  - I8 and I14 compare `legal_actions` with `reduce`. Both ask the same filter, so a bug in the filter passes both checks.
  - I19 sees a Dormant card only when an event changes it, and a pick that the effect then skips changes nothing.
- #4508 (open) checks what a Spell changes on a Unit Immune to Spells, read from its events. This one checks what a target draw aims at, including the picks that change nothing and the Evasive half. The two do not overlap.

## Proposal
Add I21 to the invariant monitor: every `target` pick is one its source may aim at.
1. A testkit seam records each random `target` draw: the source card, the seat and the picks. It records at `answer_at_random` and at the declared-target draw sites above. It follows the thread-local pattern of `crates/engine/src/testkit/seams.rs`, which the engine consults only under `#[cfg(feature = "testkit")]`.
2. `InvariantMonitor::after` drains the record and judges each pick on its own reading of the state, as I17 does. It does not call `restrictions::evasive_bars`, `immune_to_spells` or the prompt filter (the monitor's header: an oracle, not the fix restated). It flags:
   - an Evasive card face-up on the field, when the source is a Spell or a Field Spell;
   - a Unit Immune to Spells, when the source is a Spell;
   - a Dormant card, whatever the source.
3. The same judgement applies to every `target` declaration `legal_actions` lists and every open `target` prompt's options, read in `hidden` beside I13 and I15. That catches a filter bug the listing and the reducer share.
4. Random picks made by an effect, not a targeting step, are not judged. 'A random enemy' is one: R4353002 lets such a pick reach an Evasive card.
5. Each Duos duel runs the check through `DuosInvariantMonitor`, as I19 does.

## Where it lands
- `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` (I21 and the header's list of checks) and `crates/engine/src/testkit/seams.rs` (the record)
- `crates/engine/src/prompts.rs`, `random_targets.rs`, `play_steps.rs`, `cry_trigger.rs` and `play_choices.rs`: one testkit-only record call each
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` (the tests) and `crates/tools/README.md`'s `fuzz` row
- SPEC §10.7 (the fuzz); R452, R1200, R4353002, R1839000

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] I21 fails a step whose random `target` draw names a card its source may not aim at: an Evasive card in play from a Spell or Field Spell source, a Unit Immune to Spells from a Spell source, or a Dormant card. This covers a random cast's prompt (R452) and a Mayor's declared target or prompt (R1200). The message leads with `I21`, cites the ruling and names the source and the pick.
- [ ] I21 also fails a listed `target` declaration or an open `target` prompt option that offers such a card.
- [ ] The check reads keywords, zones and face-down state itself and calls none of the engine's targeting filters.
- [ ] Tests in `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` hand the check one bad pick of each kind and see it flagged. They also see these clean: a legal pick, a Unit or Trap source aiming at an Evasive card, and a random pick made by an effect.
- [ ] The seam and its record calls compile only under `testkit`, and `RULE_4_STATICS` in `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` passes unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200` and `cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --seeds 50` run clean. Any breach they find is fixed in the same pull request, or filed as its own issue and named in the report.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' invariants`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

## Size and risks
Hard (engine testkit, CLAUDE.md rule 11): about 250 to 350 lines with tests, across about eight files. The seam adds a testkit-only line at about five engine sites; a release build does not change. The daily 10,000-seed waves may go red at first on a card that still draws a pick it may not. That is the point, but each such breach needs its own fix. If a lawful exception turns up, it goes on I21's list with the ruling that allows it, as I19 keeps its own.

# Plan

## Goal

Add invariant I21 to the fuzz monitor: every random `target` draw, every listed `target` declaration, and every open `target` prompt option is one its source may aim at (R452, R1200, R4353002, R1839000, R450). Random draws are recorded through a testkit seam and judged by the oracle in `after`; listings and open prompts are judged in `hidden`; Duos runs both per duel. Tests prove each bad pick flags and each lawful pick stays clean.

## Files to touch

| Path | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/engine/src/testkit/seams.rs` | change | `RandomDrawKind` (`RandomCast`/`Mayor`), `RandomTargetDraw` struct with `of()` snapshot helper, `record_random_target_draw`, `take_random_target_draws`, `set_current_duel`/`current_duel`, extend `clear_seams` |
| `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` | change | I21 header paragraph, `unlawful_target_pick` oracle, `i21_draw_findings`, `i21_listed_findings`, `i21_prompt_findings`, wire into `before`/`after`/`hidden`/`DuosInvariantMonitor` |
| `crates/engine/src/prompts.rs` | change | `answer_at_random` gains a `RandomDrawKind` parameter; both `cast_prompt_shape` call sites pass it; one testkit-gated record call for `Target` prompts with a resolvable source |
| `crates/engine/src/play_steps.rs` | change | One testkit-gated record call after each of the two draws in `ask_repeat_targets` (Mayor `draw_picks` ~line 2511, random `random_picks` ~line 2527) |
| `crates/engine/src/cry_trigger.rs` | change | One testkit-gated record call after each draw in `ask_targets` (Mayor ~line 339, random-cast ~line 367) |
| `crates/engine/src/play_choices.rs` | change | One testkit-gated record call at the end of `with_drawn_target_picks` (~line 2404) |
| `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` | change | New `mod i21` with the tests below |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | `fuzz` row: `I1–I20` becomes `I1–I21`, add the I21 clause |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, anything under `spec/` (no new ruling: R452's last sentence already states the rule), `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` (`RULE_4_STATICS` already skips `src/testkit/` and clippy already allows `Cell`), `crates/engine/src/config.rs` (no numbers added), `crates/engine/src/duos/reduce.rs`, `apps/web`, `e2e`. ## Steps

1. In `crates/engine/src/testkit/seams.rs`, add the record (copy the `Cell<Vec<…>>` take/set shape of `WORK_HANDLERS`; `Cell` keeps the purity lint and the statics scan green). 2. In `crates/engine/src/prompts.rs`, add a `context: crate::testkit::seams::RandomDrawKind` parameter to `answer_at_random`. Pass `Mayor` at the Mayor call site (~line 1307) and `RandomCast` at the random-cast call site (~line 1355). After `let targets = in_offered_order(&probe, selection);`, add a `#[cfg(feature = "testkit")]` block that records only when `args.kind == PromptKind::Target` and `args.resume.instance_id` resolves via `find_instance`, using `RandomTargetDraw::of(sink.state, source, args.player, context, targets.clone())`.
3. In `crates/engine/src/play_steps.rs` `ask_repeat_targets`, after each draw and before the `repeat.targets.extend(picks)`, add a `#[cfg(feature = "testkit")]` record call with source `card`, seat `run.player`, `picks.clone()`, context `Mayor` (the `draw_picks` site) and `RandomCast` (the `random_picks` site).
4. In `crates/engine/src/cry_trigger.rs` `ask_targets`, do the same with source `card`, seat `run.controller`: `Mayor` at the `draw_picks` site, `RandomCast` at the `random_picks` site.
5. In `crates/engine/src/play_choices.rs` `with_drawn_target_picks`, before `Ok(out)`, add a `#[cfg(feature = "testkit")]` record call with source `card`, seat `player`, `out.clone()`, context `Mayor`.
6. In `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs`, write the oracle `fn unlawful_target_pick(state: &GameState, source_type: CardType, pick: &Selection) -> Option<(&'static str, &'static str)>`. Judge only `Selection::Instance` picks whose card `find_instance` finds on a field zone; anything else returns `None`. Return `Some` in this order: slumbering card means `("a Dormant card, which nothing may target", "R1839000")` for any source; face-up (`!preview::is_face_down`) plus layered `Evasive` (`has_keyword(&layers::unit_view(state, card).keywords, KeywordKind::Evasive`) plus source `Spell`/`FieldSpell` means `("an Evasive card in play, which Spells and Field Spells may not target", "R4353002")`; face-up plus layered `ImmuneToSpells` plus source `Spell` means `("a Unit Immune to Spells, which Spells may not target", "R450")`. Call none of `restrictions::*`, `may_target`, or `targetable_options`.
7. In the same file add `fn i21_draw_findings(state: &GameState, draws: &[RandomTargetDraw]) -> Vec<String>`, pushing one finding per unlawful Instance pick: `I21 unlawful random target: {source_id} ({source_def}) drew {pick_id} ({pick_def}) on turn {turn}: {reason} ({context.ruling()}, {rule})`, with source/pick labels from `find_instance` (`name_of`-style) falling back to the recorded ids. Add `fn i21_listed_findings(state: &GameState, viewer: PlayerId, legal: &[ActionBody]) -> Vec<String>`: for `Play` actions resolve the card and use `active_target_decls(declared_targets(state, card), modes)` with `selections_per_declaration` to judge each `Target`-kind slice; for `Activate`/`ActivatePower` resolve the card, find its ability in `subsystems::activate::abilities_of` by id, and judge that decl's `Target` slices the same way. Message: `I21 unlawful listed target: {viewer}'s {play|activate} of {source} lists {pick} on turn {turn}: {reason} ({rule})`. Add `fn i21_prompt_findings(state: &GameState) -> Vec<String>`: when `state.pending` has `kind == Target`, judge each option's `selection` with the source from `pending.resume.instance_id` (skip when unresolvable). Message: `I21 unlawful target offered: prompt {id} of {source} offers {pick} on turn {turn}: {reason} ({rule})`. Make all three `pub` like the other helpers the tests use.
8. Wire the monitor. In `InvariantMonitor::before`, first drain-and-discard `take_random_target_draws()` and set the duel marker to `None` (this drops draws that I8/I14 probe reductions record between steps). Split `after` into `after` (drains, keeps draws with `duel.is_none()`, delegates) and `after_with_draws(&mut self, events, state, draws)` that runs the existing body plus `i21_draw_findings`. In `hidden`, after the existing per-seat checks, extend with `i21_listed_findings(state, viewer, &legal)` per seat and `i21_prompt_findings(state)` once. In `DuosInvariantMonitor::before`, call the per-duel `before` first, then set the marker to `Some(seat.duel())` for `Duel` bodies and `None` for `Pass`/`Concede`. In `DuosInvariantMonitor::after`, drain once, partition draws by tag (`Some(d)` to duel `d`; untagged draws to the duel holding their `source_id`, else the duel holding their first Instance pick, else skipped), and call each duel monitor's `after_with_draws` with its events and its draws; reset the marker to `None`. Update the module header (`twenty` to `twenty-one`, an I21 paragraph after I20's, `before`/`after`/`hidden` line) and the Duos `after`/`hidden` doc lines to name I21.
9. Update the `fuzz` row in `crates/tools/README.md`: `I1–I20` to `I1–I21`, and append to the invariant list that I21 holds every random `target` draw, listed `target` declaration, and open `target` prompt option to R452/R1200/R4353002/R1839000/R450, read off keywords, zones, and face-down state.
10. Add `mod i21` to `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` (copy the `mod i19` shape). Build boards with `playing()`/`put()`/`slot()`; grant `Keyword::Evasive`/`Keyword::ImmuneToSpells` and set `slumber` as `effects_cast.rs` does; register one inline Spell script declaring `TargetDecl::target(1, 1, json!({"of": ["unit", "hero"]}))` for the listing test. Write the tests in the Tests section. Run the commands there plus `cargo fmt --check`.

## Tests

All in `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs`, `mod i21`:

- `i21_random_cast_draw_naming_an_evasive_unit_is_flagged`: draw `{RandomCast, Spell}` naming an Evasive field unit gives exactly one `i21_draw_findings` entry leading with `I21`, citing `R4353002`, naming source and pick.
- `i21_random_cast_draw_naming_an_immune_or_dormant_unit_is_flagged`: one draw naming an Immune unit and one naming a Dormant card give two findings citing `R450` and `R1839000`.
- `i21_mayor_declared_draw_naming_a_dormant_card_is_flagged`: `{Mayor, Spell}` draw naming a Dormant card cites `R1200` and `R1839000`.
- `i21_legal_draw_is_clean`: Spell draw naming a plain unit gives none.
- `i21_unit_or_trap_source_may_aim_at_an_evasive_card`: `Unit` and `Trap` sources naming the Evasive unit give none.
- `i21_unrecorded_effect_picks_are_not_judged`: `after(&[], &state)` with an Evasive unit on the field and an empty record gives no `I21` finding.
- `i21_recorded_draws_flag_through_after_then_drain`: record one bad draw via seams, `after` flags it, the next `after` is clean.
- `i21_listed_declaration_offering_an_unlawful_pick_is_flagged`: fabricated `Play` of the inline Spell naming the Evasive unit gives one `i21_listed_findings` entry; the same action naming a plain unit gives none.
- `i21_open_prompt_offering_an_unlawful_pick_is_flagged`: crafted `state.pending` `Target` prompt offering the Evasive unit makes `hidden()` return an `I21` entry; offering only a plain unit keeps `hidden()` free of `I21`.

Commands:

```sh
cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' invariants
cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance statics_the_pure_crates_hold_only_the_statics_rule_4_allows
cargo fmt --check
cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200
cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --seeds 50
```

## Done when

- [ ] A step whose random `target` draw names an Evasive unit from a Spell/Field Spell source, an Immune unit from a Spell source, or a Dormant card from any source fails with an `I21` message citing the ruling and naming source and pick, for both `RandomCast` (R452) and `Mayor` (R1200) contexts.
- [ ] A listed `target` declaration or an open `target` prompt option offering such a card fails the same way.
- [ ] The oracle reads keywords, zones, and face-down state itself and calls no targeting filter.
- [ ] The new tests flag each bad pick and stay clean for a legal pick, Unit/Trap sources on Evasive, and unrecorded effect picks.
- [ ] The seam and its six record calls compile only under `testkit`; `RULE_4_STATICS` passes unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200` and `cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --seeds 50` run clean; any breach is fixed in the pull request or filed as its own issue and named.
- [ ] The listed test, clippy, and fmt commands pass.

## Risks

- The oracle judges post-step state, so a pick lawful at draw time but unlawful after (or the reverse) is misjudged; I17 accepts the same trade and no mid-step keyword flip of this kind is known.
- I8/I14 probe reductions record draws too; they are never judged because `before` drains the record at each step start, and their draws come from the same filtered options, so judging them would agree anyway.
- Duos instance ids can collide across duels, so attribution uses the duel marker set in `Duos before`, not ids; untagged draws (begin/settle, which draw no targets) fall back to source-then-pick lookup and are documented as unexpected.
- `hidden` now maps listed actions to declaration slices; the cost is the same class as the I13/I15 reads beside it and stays behind the existing stride.
- I14 branch states are not given the I21 listing check; the played path plus the daily waves cover it.

## Open questions

None.

- - `i21_legal_draw_is_clean`: Spell draw naming a plain unit gives none.
- - `i21_unit_or_trap_source_may_aim_at_an_evasive_card`: `Unit` and `Trap` sources naming the Evasive unit give none.
- - `i21_unrecorded_effect_picks_are_not_judged`: `after(&[], &state)` with an Evasive unit on the field and an empty record gives no `I21` finding.
- - `i21_recorded_draws_flag_through_after_then_drain`: record one bad draw via seams, `after` flags it, the next `after` is clean.
- - `i21_listed_declaration_offering_an_unlawful_pick_is_flagged`: fabricated `Play` of the inline Spell naming the Evasive unit gives one `i21_listed_findings` entry; the same action naming a plain unit gives none.
- - `i21_open_prompt_offering_an_unlawful_pick_is_flagged`: crafted `state.pending` `Target` prompt offering the Evasive unit makes `hidden()` return an `I21` entry; offering only a plain unit keeps `hidden()` free of `I21`.

- ```sh
- cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' invariants
- cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance statics_the_pure_crates_hold_only_the_statics_rule_4_allows
- cargo fmt --check
- cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200
- cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --seeds 50
- ```

- - The oracle judges post-step state, so a pick lawful at draw time but unlawful after (or the reverse) is misjudged; I17 accepts the same trade and no mid-step keyword flip of this kind is known.
